summary: No 2026 framework does seamless cross-server entity handoff for Rust+Rapier+voxel+QUIC. Build in-house; reuse patterns only. See options for the full 12-platform verdict matrix.

options.name: SpacetimeDB
options.fit: Sandboxed WASM reducers cannot host native Rapier; one DB=one node; cross-shard handoff DIY. Best language/license fit (Rust/BSL/self-host); study deterministic replay.

options.name: Nakama
options.fit: Go not Rust; match on one node; matchSignal handoff is a rare exception; presence-replication pattern useful for peer_registry/observer.

options.name: Rivet
options.fit: Apache-2 Rust self-host durable actors; good orchestrator/lifecycle substrate but no live entity migration; you still own handoff.

options.name: Edgegap
options.fit: Fleet/placement orchestration only; runs your Rust shard binary; no handoff; use if you outgrow k3d.

options.name: Improbable SpatialOS
options.fit: Dead (sold to Yuga 2026); was THE entity-handoff product; study chunk-boundary authority lessons + failure modes only.

options.name: Hadean Aether Engine
options.fit: Pivoted to defense; unavailable, not Rust/self-hostable for games; load-balancing lessons only.

options.name: Hathora
options.fit: Defunct May 2026 (pivot to voice AI); was fleet orchestration only.

options.name: Colyseus
options.fit: Node.js only, no Rust/Rapier; room-based, no seamless cross-room handoff; no QUIC.

options.name: Croquet/Multisynq
options.fit: Client-side deterministic VMs, no server-authoritative sim; cannot host trusted Rapier; DePIN/crypto.

options.name: Ambient
options.fit: Closest Rust+WASM match but runtime paused indefinitely; not a handoff engine; unacceptable dependency.

options.name: Dojo/MUD (onchain)
options.fit: Blockchain; latency/cost incompatible with real-time physics.

options.name: PlayFab/EOS + lightyear
options.fit: PlayFab/EOS = matchmaking/fleet only, no handoff. lightyear (Rust/Bevy) Rooms+visibility interest management transferable to dual-shard compositing/observer; you build handoff.
